instruction.text: This is a map of Brazil. Select the rainforest to learn more.

hint.label: Did you know?
hint.text: The Amazon Rainforest is so large that the UK would fit inside it over 20 times!

atoms.b: The Amazon is the world’s largest ((snowy ++tropical)) rainforest. It spans 9 countries, and covers around 40% of Brazil.
It is one of the most biodiverse ((mountains ++ecosystems)) in the world and holds around 10% of all known animal and plant species on Earth.
Here you can also find the Amazon River, which is the longest river in South America, and one of the ((shortest ++longest)) rivers in the world.
The river is home to many interesting animals, such as electric eels, giant ((ocean ++river)) otters, pink river dolphins and piranhas.

trainers.instruction: Read the text and select the matching image.

atoms.a: The Pantanal is one of the world’s largest freshwater wetlands, and consists of many lakes, swamps and marshes.
It is home to the highest concentration of jaguars anywhere in the world.
The waterways of the Pantanal are also home to millions of caimans.

hint.text: Caimans are semi-aquatic reptiles native to Central and South America. They are in the same family as alligators, but they are typically much smaller.
hint.label: Caimans

atoms.a: Cattle farming is very popular here, and the region is one of Brazil’s biggest producers of beef.

instruction.text: The Port of Itaqui is one of Brazil’s busiest ports. Match each product to the correct image.

feedback.finish: Brazil’s economy is largely dependent on exporting goods such as these all around the world. Other key exports include sugar, coffee, wood and beef.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: More than 87% of Brazil’s population live in cities, with most people living along its massive coastline.
In contrast, the north-western regions in the Amazon are much less populated and are home to many indigenous people, whose tribes are thousands of years old.
Located on the south-east coast, Rio de Janeiro is Brazil’s second-largest city and is famous for its beaches, carnival and iconic Christ the Redeemer statue.
With a population of around 12 million people, São Paolo is the most populated city in both Brazil and South America. It is crucial to the country’s economy, business and global trade.
